entries.title: Keenan's repeat involvement; Pollard's receiving gap
entries.question: Does the evidence beyond last week support retaining these two salary slots?
entries.why_it_matters: Tuesday's replacements were based partly on single-game opportunity. Repeated involvement and the kind of touches matter under full PPR.
findings: Keenan's inspected log shows9,9,11 targets over his last three appearances, spanning a win and two losses. That supports involvement beyond one game but does not establish a weekly target floor.
Pollard's last five carry totals after Week1 are14,17,16,14,19. His last two games have no catches on one target each; the selection primarily purchases rushing opportunity.
Cleveland's recap shows defensive resistance after Baltimore's opening two drives, while its own offense conceded three first-half sacks. Neither fact is a league-adjusted Week7 prediction.
The current same-model table favors Braelon17.3 versus Pollard12.4. The $600 switch fits exactly at$50,000, but Hall remainsQ and the table's split assumptions are unknown.
entries.interpretation: Hold Keenan with stronger historical involvement support. Retain Pollard provisionally for the observed rushing lead, while reducing confidence in any PPR-floor description. A contrary model estimate is a useful challenge, not a substitute for qualifying availability.
alternatives: Braelon for Pollard uses the full$600 remaining and may be preferable if Hall is ruled out.
A more expensive RB requires a receiving/other-slot saving; cheaper uncertain volume can merely relocate the same role risk.
uncertainty: Keenan's passing volume, health and route share versus Minnesota remain uncertain; no route metric was retrieved.
Pollard/Spears allocation and Cleveland injured defenders' final status remain unresolved.
External model assumptions about Hall are not disclosed by the inspected table.
entries.lineup_effect: No player changes: $49,400/$600left. Keep Keenan and Pollard; retain the weakness openly. Pollard plus Titans DST share exposure to favorable Tennessee game conditions. One coherent SPAGS snapshot now provides133.1 external projected total on this new record only.
change_triggers: Official Hall absence returns Braelon to serious consideration at exactly$50,000; return/split evidence determines whether that alternative's model estimate applies.
Verified Colts role/availability change weakens Keenan; current three-game involvement is evidence, not a floor.
carry_forward: Check Hall's official Week7 participation/status before deciding whether the exactly$50,000 Braelon alternative is better supported.
Compare Keenan's role with team pass volume and other Colts targets; do not demand a repeated9-target minimum.
Evaluate Pollard's rushing opportunity separately from efficiency, TDs and receiving production after games.
Provisional research lesson: same salary or legal budget does not make two opportunity assumptions equally sound.

expectations.support: Last three appearances show9,9,11 targets in the inspected data log.
expectations.uncertainty: Passing volume, coverage and health may change. No repeated9-target floor asserted.

expectations.subject: Tony Pollard
expectations.statement: If available, Pollard retains the lead share of Titans RB carries; the selection does not depend on a newly expanded receiving role.
expectations.support: The game log shows14,17,16,14,19 carries after Week1 and no catches in the last two games.
expectations.uncertainty: Game script and Spears usage may reduce carries. Cleveland defensive resistance remains a risk.
expectations.challenge: Spears or another RB taking the rushing lead, or Pollard losing meaningful participation, would undermine the hold.
expectations.observe: Compare each Titans RB's carries, targets and receiving work; separate opportunity from rushing efficiency/TDs. Examine script only with inspected play evidence.

entries.title: Vacated opportunity is not an automatic replacement role
entries.question: Do the cheap Rams alternatives justify changing this whole lineup, and does Giants QB uncertainty change Nabers?
entries.why_it_matters: The low price of a listed player can distract from actual availability or uncertain target distribution. Role assumptions affect concentration as well as cost.
findings: The official Rams update confirms Adams6-10weeks. NFL reporting states Ferguson cannot come offIR untilWeek8; the official salary pool also marks himIR.

Mumpfield is priced$3,200. FTN attributes27snaps/3targets toWeek6 and notes Atwell, Whittington and TEs as competing recipients. Those figures are attributed secondary analysis, not independently verified route data.
The model table has no inspected coherent projection for Mumpfield. No zero or agent-invented estimate was substituted.

The official Giants tracker still describes an unresolved QB decision and records Nabers29catches/398yards across three games. No confirmed McCarthy start or measured receiver-specific uplift established.
entries.interpretation: Keep Puka as the established Rams receiving choice without assuming he absorbs all Adams targets. Watch Mumpfield rather than replacing stronger observed Colts involvement with an unverified role. Exclude Ferguson fromWeek7 consideration. Keep Nabers on involvement evidence, not a desperation-quarter quarterback extrapolation.
alternatives: Mumpfield for Keenan lowers lineup cost to$47,800/$2,200left, but adds a second Rams receiver and allocation uncertainty; no automatic upgrade is claimed.
Ferguson for LaPorta would lower cost to$47,100/$2,900left, but is rejected as unavailable forWeek7.
A supported later rotation/availability report could justify reallocating savings across RB and WR, rather than evaluating a cheap receiver in isolation.
uncertainty: Actual Rams post-Adams rotation, Atwell availability and coverage allocation remain unresolved.
Loss of Adams can increase Puka's opportunity while reducing offensive efficiency; no net point uplift is invented.
Giants starter/protection decision still open in the inspected tracker.
entries.lineup_effect: Hold Puka/Nabers/LaPorta/Keenan and the other five. No new Rams stack or cheap-IR substitution. All nine original salaries stay at$49,400. The strongest countercase remains a better qualified RB alternative plus a cheaper receiving role.
change_triggers: Rams rotation/Atwell reports establish an actual receiving role for Mumpfield; Ferguson remains excluded from thisWeek7 candidate set.
Giants QB/protection news changes Nabers risk without treating desperation volume as normal.
carry_forward: Revisit Mumpfield only when a substantiated role or actual rotation supports the salary tradeoff; more vacated snaps are not guaranteed targets.
Ferguson is a separate Week8 question, not an eligibleWeek7 fix.
Observe Nabers' actual QB and targets; a later substitution is a condition to evaluate, not a retroactive pregame justification.
Source-quality note: FTN's15-point Rams statement conflicts with the official16; use the official result.
